title: Crucial Conversations
author: Kerry Patterson, Joseph Grenny, Ron McMillan, Al Switzler
text: Do you wonder how to improve your communication skills? Don't look further. This can help you navigate in critical and hard conversations. If you want to read one book about soft skills, this is it!

title: The Coaching Habit
author: Michael Bungay Stanier
text: Is teaching others part of your job? It explains nicely how you can teach by asking certain questions.

title: Radical Candor
author: Kim Scott
text: While it's mostly focussed for team leaders, one can get many things out of it. Most prominent is giving honest feedback. There are many other good ideas in this book, I can highly recommend it.

title: Drive
author: Daniel H. Pink
text: THE book about motivation. The author names the three elements: Purpose, Autonomy and Mastery to be the key for great motivation.

title: The Five Dysfunctions of a Team (Comic Book Edition)
author: Patrick Lencioni
text: If you feel that something is not right in your team, you might take a glimpse into this one.

title: Start with Why
author: Simon Sinek
text: This book could be much shorter, but still contains some very powerful and valuable concepts.

title: Better Allies
author: Karen Catlin
text: I care a lot about diversity. This book helped me picking up some inspiration and concrete action items to be more inclusive.

title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
author: Martin Kleppmann
text: Already a classic. Explains to a very detailed level how to design data intensive systems. This has to potential to bring you from zero to hero.

title: Functional Programming in Scala
author: Paul Chiusano, Rúnar Bjarnason
text: The famous red book. Very useful primer to get you started with advanced functional programming in Scala

title: The Pragmatic Programmer
author: David Thomas, Andrew Hunt
text: This was recently re-released. The old version was the most important programming book I've ever read. Picked up many good ideas / insights on how to self-improve as programmer.

title: Advanced Scala with Cats
author: Noel Welsh, Dave Gurnell
text: Free ebook by Underscore.io. It is a perfect primer on how to apply Cats to make your Scala code better

title: Functional Programming for Mortals
author: Sam Halliday
text: I liked reading this after Advanced Scala with Cats. It showed me how to structure applications and re-enforced some ideas.
